title: World of Warcraft: Forever won't destroy what made the old classes so satisfying by modernizing them into oblivion: 'The level of mechanical complexity found in the beta classes is indicative of our intentions'
summary: You will wait patiently for your next ability and you will learn to love it.
body: Part of World of Warcraft: Forever's charm is that combat is considerably slower than the regular version of the MMO. It's the kind of game where you'll spend 38 seconds hitting a scorpion because there are so few buttons to press in the early stages of your journey. Classes in WoW's past were simple, but had small quirks to them that you'd pick up over time. Melee classes, for example, can squeeze abilities in between their auto attacks to maximize their damage output. You'd never care about this if fights only took 10 seconds, like they do in WoW today, but back then you had to use all that time in more drawn-out battles for something . The WoW: Forever beta has reminded me how satisfying it is to play a class that isn't built like Whac-A-Mole, where the challenge is to hit the right buttons the moment they start to glow. There's a rhythm to WoW's old classes and I'm delighted to hear that Blizzard fully intends to maintain it in WoW: Forever. Blizzard developers told TechRadar that they want "to err on the side of simpler classes, but with engaging depth," and that all of it will align with its guiding principle of staying true to the old MMO's "core design, pacing, and tone." …

title: Can you beat General Lothaire in Valor Mortis?
summary: Beat this big boss first time.
body: Key deets ⚔️ If you beat General Lothaire you get the General's Catalyst Clot, 10k catalysts, and the Torn-Banner achievement. ⚔️ You only have one attempt to beat him, since if you die, a cutscene will play and the boss will disappear. ⚔️ If you hit ALT + F4 the moment you die, I found you can load in just before the boss arena to try again. General Lothaire, The Eagle-Bearer, is the first boss in Valor Mortis and is one of those classic starting soulslike fights you're really not supposed to win. The odds are very much against you, especially as you only have one attempt. Dying will start a cutscene where Lucjan appears to save you and provides a bit of an info dump about the world, but the boss will disappear. While spending way too long beating Lothaire to find out what happens, I realised you can actually ALT + F4 the moment you die, and it generally puts you outside the boss arena when you load back in, letting you attempt the fight again. If you beat General Lothaire, you'll get: 10k catalysts (effectively souls in this game) The General's Catalyst Clot (which gives a further 10k) It's a pretty big bonus in terms of initial levelling. Valor Mortis also doesn't have boss wea…

title: How to equip ambers in Valor Mortis
summary: Slot these rare gems to gain passive bonuses and abilities.
body: (Image credit: One More Level) Key deets 💎 Ambers are precious gems you equip to gain passive bonuses and abilities. 💎 You can slot them at the level up menu with any lantern. 💎 You unlock a new slot every ten levels. You'll most likely find your first amber in Valor Mortis before you're actually able to equip it. The game has a fairly simplistic skill tree that focuses around passive buffs, so the ambers you equip are more what add a bit of spice to your build. You can equip an amber once you reach Level 5 by leveling up at any lantern. When you enter the level up menu, you'll notice that a slot with a + symbol has unlocked on the bottom layer—click on this and select the amber you want to equip, and don't worry, you can swap them at any time. After this, you'll unlock a new slots every ten levels at: Slot two : Level 15 Slot three : Level 25 Slot four : Level 35 Slot five : Level 45 This means there are five amber slots overall. You'll generally get new ambers from quests and chests, and any amber you already own will level up to provide a more powerful passive bonus when you acquire a copy of it. title: AMD has reportedly already raised GDDR6 prices for its graphics card partners, so you'll find no solace from spiking GPU prices with Team Red
summary: Getting worse before it gets better.
body: We all know RAM and SSD prices have been significantly impacted by the memory supply crisis. But it's easy for some to forget just how much dedicated memory modern graphics cards rock these days. And when I say 'some' I mean those not still trying to hunt down a reasonably priced Nvidia RTX 5090. Alas, it sounds like the broader situation shows no signs of improvement. Unfortunately for its Add-in Board partners, AMD has reportedly raised its prices for the GDDR6 memory that comes with its GPUs. According to sources on Chinese forum Boardchannels, the price increase took effect October 1 (via Benchlife ). If AIBs are having to pay more for AMD GPUs, they'll likely also raise their prices and pass the expense on to the consumer. Long story short, PC gamers will likely have to spend more on team red's wares in the near future. title: Behold, the $3,000 keyboard that is also actually a powerful AI PC I would hate to spill my coffee on

body: As you may already suspect, the ZX Spectrum was a bit before my time. Still, a whole home computer crammed inside a relatively svelte keyboard is something with timeless appeal. HP's Eliteboard series debuted with the G1a at CES 2026 , which boasted a Kraken Point APU and a Radeon 860M integrated GPU (this made it roughly as powerful as the Steam Deck ). Already the company has come out with a refresh in the form of the HP EliteBoard G2a, which is pitched as a 'Next Gen AI PC' complete with a Copilot key. This follow-up sequesters some serious hardware inside its svelte frame for AI-geared workloads. Within what I must admit just looks like a regular office keyboard, there is up to 32 GB of RAM and an AMD Gorgon Point CPU. body: Arc Raiders ' new outpost system arrived with the Frozen Trail update, and like many I'm sure, I pretty much ignored the entire furniture aspect of it. Crafting furniture in your Arc Raiders outpost actually gives you hundreds of extra storage slots for items and weapons and it's fairly easy to unlock, you just need to: Reach level 18 to start the Sheltered Retreat project. title: Gigabyte deletes blog post on Intel LGA1700 chips in early 2027, but it can't put the cat back in the bag
summary: Looks like Gigabyte made an error when it posted about Intel's upcoming LGA1700 chips last week.
body: Last week, Gigabyte suggested Intel was working on a new wave of LGA1700 processors —likely a Raptor Lake refresh for expanded DDR4 support during these memory-constrained times. It has even been busy releasing BIOS files for B760 and H610 motherboards to ensure full compatibility once those chips arrive, which it expected was around "early 2027". This week, Gigabyte has scrubbed all mention of those forthcoming chips, removed the blog post, and replaced it with another that's much less explicit. Here's the important bit from Gigabyte's blog post last week: "Built on socket LGA1700 and expected to launch in early 2027, the new processors bring fresh performance to an established platform, and Gigabyte users can be ready from day one." That's now been deleted . Gigabyte posted a new blog post on October 13 on the same topic. It notes that Gigabyte has expanded LGA1700 processor support across Z790, B760, and H610 motherboards—adding Z790 chipsets to the list. Notably, this one lacks any explicit mention of upcoming Intel chips: "[Gigabyte] today announced a new BIOS update that delivers more comprehensive LGA1700 processor support across its entire lineup of Intel Z790, B760 and H6…

title: People are being robbed of crypto by a tiny chip implanted in their hardware, with $100 million said to have been stolen already
summary: Investigation of the "draining incident of Oct 9th" is ongoing.
body: I never got into crypto, but when I was considering doing so I was pretty quickly convinced that I should use a hardware wallet to store my private keys, as these are usually considered to pose less of a risk of being hacked and stolen than storing everything online. But alas, it seems one of the most reputable hardware wallets on the market has fallen victim of a supply chain attack (via a reseller) that's reportedly left some users short of a tidy collective sum of at least $86 million and, according to YFarmX's calculations, potentially over $100 million . Ledger, the hardware wallet maker in question, has since said that as part of its investigation into the reports of stolen crypto, it can indeed confirm that "one of the impacted users' devices contained an unauthorised hardware implant." The company also says , "To date, all confirmed cases related to the disclosed draining incident of Oct 9th, 2026, involve devices sold through the Southeast Asia reseller CryptoBilis." Ledger says CryptoBillis confirms it has ceased all sales of the wallet until the ongoing investigation is concluded. title: How to turn off your backpack light in Arc Raiders
summary: Use the new feature to get real sneaky.
body: You're looking for the "Emissive" option (Image credit: Embark Studios) Key deets 💡 Arc Raiders now has an option to turn off the light on your backpack. 💡 This is the "Emissive" toggle in each backpack's cosmetic menu. Arc Raiders has made lots of new tweaks and additions with Frozen Trail's 2.0 update, but one long-requested change of significant note is that you can turn off the light on your backpacks. To do this, you need to: Select the "Raider" menu. Enter "Customization" on the bottom left of the screen. Go to the "Style" menu at the top. Choose "Backpack" on the left side. Toggle the Emissive option to "off". As you'll see, while looking at the backpack, the light will disappear and reappear as you toggle this, though where exactly the light is varies from pack to pack. This should help you be a little sneakier, though it might make your character a bit harder to spot in some of the game's darkest areas. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together

summary: Just because I'm sneaking around doesn't mean I don't want to look my best.
body: I remember being a kid and wishing I had shoes that lit up. I know now that I was a fool. If I festooned myself with garish lights, how would I scavenge for supplies in a frozen wasteland without being spotted by strangers who may or may not kill me before I can use my grappling hook to get away? This isn't a real problem I have, nor is it a real problem Arc Raiders players will have anymore, since your backpack now has an emissive toggle. That's one of many little overhauls that arrived in Embark Studios' popular extraction shooter Thursday, and you can read all about the rest in the 2.0 patch notes . If you've not been tuned into the extraction world as of late, you did indeed read that right: Arc Raiders has gotten a big shakeup with the Frozen Trails update , which comes bearing snowy mountains and grappling hooks. But that's not what's exciting about patch notes—the best part of combing through each little bullet point is seeing all those long-awaited bug fixes and little quality-of-life changes like the aforementioned emissive toggle for backpacks. title: The developer of an AI-powered driving instruction simulator is spending $1,000 per day just to keep its demo running
summary: Teach My Little Sister How to Drive centres around a costly chatbot.
body: One of the many ways AI will (supposedly) revolutionise the games industry is facilitating highly reactive NPCs via LLM-powered chatbots. Yet so far, only a handful of games like Where Winds Meet have attempted to implement the tech, and the results have been less than spectacular. But there might also be another reason why relatively few games feature LLM-powered NPCs, which is that powering such chatbots can be costly, as recently demonstrated by the developers of an upcoming driving instructor simulator As reported by FRVR (via Kotaku ) Teach My Little Sister How To Drive is a comic simulation game in which you coach your virtual sibling on driving technique from the comfort of the passenger seat. The twist is that behind your sister's dinner-plate eyes is an LLM chatbot (currently powered by an OpenAI model, though the developers intend to use Gemini for the final release) In the role of instructor, players can both converse with the chatbot and issue vocal instructions such as "turn left here", to which the bot will respond accordingly.
